# You are onboarding this project to Grafz

Grafz is a semantic memory API for AI apps and agents: ingest conversations, documents, files, and URLs; get semantic search, extracted facts, and context back. Every call is scoped to a specific user using their `GRAFZ_API_KEY`.

## What you can call

| Operation | Endpoint | Use when |
|---|---|---|
| Ingest memory | POST /api/ingest | Save facts, context, or raw chunks to the semantic graph |
| Search memories | GET /api/memory?q={query}&limit={limit} | Find extracted facts via high-dimensional vector similarity |
| Create API Key | POST /api/keys | Programmatically generate a new key for a user |

Full API reference for agents is available at: https://grafzz-flame.vercel.app/api/docs

Now work the steps below in order. Do not skip ahead. Stop where a step says to.

## Step 1 — Credentials

API key env var: `GRAFZ_API_KEY` (never hardcode it, never print it back).

If that reads `YOUR_GRAFZ_API_KEY`, ask the user to log into the Grafz dashboard (https://grafzz-flame.vercel.app), create an API Key from the sidebar, export it as `GRAFZ_API_KEY`, and tell you when it is set. Wait for confirmation.

## Step 2 — Install the docs MCP server, then brief the user

Add this MCP server to your client to interact with Grafz directly: 
`https://grafzz-flame.vercel.app/api/mcp`

It serves tools to `search_grafz_memories` and `ingest_grafz_memory`. Prefer its answers over prior knowledge for anything related to the user's semantic graph.

Then give the user a short rundown of what Grafz can do for THIS project, using the table above.

## Step 3 — Scan this repo for integration points

If this directory has application source, read enough to understand it, then map findings against this table. Cite exact files and lines. If the repo is empty or docs-only, say so and skip to Step 5.

| Code pattern | Replace / augment with |
|---|---|
| Chat or agent loop with no memory between sessions | Add each exchange via `POST /api/ingest`, search before the model answers via `GET /api/memory` |
| Full conversation history stuffed into the prompt | Retrieved context from `GET /api/memory` instead of replaying everything |
| Homegrown embeddings pipeline (pgvector, pinecone, chroma) | `POST /api/ingest` + `GET /api/memory`, no pipeline to maintain |
| RAG over files or docs sites | Ingest raw chunks, search with a limit to ground responses |
| Multi-tenant SaaS serving many end users | One `GRAFZ_API_KEY` per end user; never share or cross-query keys |

## Step 4 — Propose, then get approval before touching code

Present findings as a numbered list: file + line range, the endpoint(s) involved, one line on why it is an improvement. Ask which to implement. Do not modify files until the user approves specific items.

When implementing, use standard HTTP REST calls with the API key in the header:

```javascript
const res = await fetch("https://grafzz-flame.vercel.app/api/memory?q=hello", {
  headers: { "Authorization": `Bearer ${process.env.GRAFZ_API_KEY}` }
});
const data = await res.json();
```

## Step 5 — Suggest uses tailored to this project

Only if Step 3 found no application code: propose 3-5 concrete places in the user's stack where a memory layer would save effort, each tied to a specific endpoint from the table. Propose, do not build.
